title: Flow prioritization failsafe and early deferral
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement an early-deferral path that proactively deprioritizes and defers non-critical requests at the routing layer when fleet headroom is forecasted to fall below guaranteed throughput thresholds. This feature sits between the ingress throttle and tenant-level admission and aims to preserve hard throughput commitments for SLO-bound traffic while reducing downstream autoscaler thrash and GPU oversubscription. Work includes: routing policy changes, lightweight per-request cost heuristics, a soft deferral queue with bounded time window, metrics + tracing hooks, and compatibility with existing fallback-to-hosted policies.
acceptance_criteria: New routing policy can mark requests as 'early-defer' within the first 5ms of admission decision
Defer queue must have configurable max latency (default 300ms) and bounded memory footprint
Requests marked early-defer are re-evaluated and retried or routed to fallback without violating tenant throughput guarantees
No measurable increase (>1%) in 95th percentile latency for high-priority lanes under load tests
End-to-end e2e test and chaos scenario validating autoscaler interaction are added to CI
comments: 2026-03-02: Kickoff sync — aligned on goals with PM and Observability. Decided early-deferral should be reversible and observable per-request.
2026-03-04: Design review with Runtime — agreed to use a lightweight scoring function based on estimated token cost, model variant and tenant SLA tier.
2026-03-06: Trade-off noted: stronger early-deferral reduces autoscaler churn but increases tail latency for deferred requests. We will expose a config knob and safe defaults.
2026-03-08: PR draft created for routing changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 — initial admission hook and metrics.

2026-03-10: QA report: loadrunner scenarios show 18% reduction in autoscaler scale-ups during short bursts for test tenants, but one regression for low-priority embeddings path. Added a follow-up sub-task.
2026-03-12: Security review triage — no secrets involved; KMS/HSM unaffected. Marked security_review_required=false. Need compliance note for audit logs retention.
rollout_plan: Canary in staging: enable early-defer for 5 internal test tenants (2 days)
Canary in production: 1% traffic for low-risk accounts, monitor throughput SLOs (48 hours)
Gradual ramp to 25% with throttling safe-guard and auto-revert if SLO violation detected
Full enable after 2 weeks with config visibility in Console and opt-out per-tenant
decisions: Use a simple additive score combining estimated token cost and SLA weight rather than ML model for initial rollout
Deferred requests will be queued at ingress rather than at GPU worker to avoid KV cache fragmentation
Expose two knobs: defer_threshold and max_deferral_ms; default conservative values chosen to prioritize SLOs
